_notes: Single config for the response-only four-arm hardware campaign; campaign.py is the entry point.
Every relative path below is relative to defense4/timing/case4_architecture.
ARMS. The four arms share ONE build, one path and one endpoint fixture (same ports, same READ range, same
fixture delay). Two independent feature bits select them: T (timing) is a LIVE toggle on an installed
composite (hw/set_enabled.py, no reinstall); padding is a POLICY ROW, not a build property: the E table
Egress.conn carries an `enable` field written at install time from response_path_cp's pad_enable. The two
padding-off arms are therefore the SAME program with the padding policy row off, not a different binary.
BLOCKED (TODO, hw/ owner): hw/bringup_composite.py has no flag that writes pad_enable=0 (hw/rows.py calls
cp.e_conn_rows with its default pad_enable=True). Until the installer grows one (campaign.py looks for
`padding_installer_flag` below in the installer source), `run` REFUSES any arm with padding 0 and says so;
`run --arms size_only,combined` runs the two padding-on arms today.
BRING-UPS. N does not re-arm after a connection and a closed tuple sits in TIME-WAIT for 60 s, so a second
connection on an installed tuple fails. trial_mode per_trial_cold (default): EVERY trial is its own cold
bring-up (swap, restore ports, install, T, snapshot, run, snapshot, teardown) on a NEW master port taken from
traffic.master_port_range, incrementing per trial; arms that share a build still get a fresh bring-up per
trial. trial_mode one_connection: one bring-up and one connection per arm with reads_per_trial x
trials_per_arm READs (the persistent-connection mode). Cold swap, not a live re-install: the installer
refuses an existing manifest and a re-install on a dirtied daemon is unrehearsed.
BINDING. Each build's `hashes` are checked three ways before anything runs: config == the build's compile
manifest.json artifact_sha256 == the files under out_dir. A null slot is filled from the manifest; a
placeholder or malformed value is an error. endpoint.binary_sha256 / lib_sha256 cannot be derived offline:
TODO pin them (command in the `endpoint._pin_with` field) before `run`; validate fails until they are set.
SHAPING. All hold-queue and blocker-queue rates default to 0 (unshaped, the production baseline). Set the
chosen rates here; the requested values are passed to the installer and to snapshot_counters, and the
ACHIEVED (hardware-quantized) rates read back in each snapshot are copied into campaign_run.json.
K. The installer's --k is 2*k generator tokens per trigger; production uses --k 2 (installer default and
hw/t_config.py pktgen_ops, count = 2*k); it is NOT 32.
Timing: readiness/cap sit above the fixture delay (25 ms) so the delayed child response arrives before the
readiness deadline and the normal commit/release path is observable (audit defect D).

production._note: The state observed before every run and restored many times on 2026-10-11. `run` reads the running program from ps before touching anything and refuses unless it equals `program`; the $PORT snapshot used for every port replay is TAKEN at the start of the run from that program (live_snapshot.py), never a stale file. Restore = cold swap to launch_script, restore_ports.py, switch_slot.py relay (if relay_slot), Vision restore, then the ping must succeed.
